section: Load data and keep only station, data, and species
end_anchor: dplyr::select(sample_id, major_area, year, month, catch, species_code)
grain_in: STATION_BS: one row per sampling occasion (sample_id); bagseine: one row per catch record (sample_id x species_code)
grain_out: station: one row per sampling occasion (sample_id x major_area x year x month); data: one row per catch record (sample_id x species_code)
operation: Loads the two objects from disk and builds the two working tables; the region's true first statement is load("data.Rdata"), which cannot be an anchor because it carries a trailing comment; the column selections are absorbed as subsetting, but the filter on station is a population change, and note that data is NOT filtered on major_area, so the rare-species screen downstream sees records from areas outside 1:8 that never enter the analysis
settings: station restricted to major_area %in% 1:8; data keeps catch and species_code only; no filter on data
na_behavior: A row with major_area NA is dropped by the filter without comment (NA %in% 1:8 is FALSE); missing catch values are carried forward untouched here
notes: The code up to this point was copied and pasted from the "b" code. I made some changes, but I confirmed they didn't affect the outputs.

grain_in: one row per catch record (sample_id x species_code)
grain_out: one row per catch record (sample_id x species_code), species set reduced
operation: Counts, for each species, the number of records with positive catch (count with wt = (catch > 0) sums logicals) and drops every species with 5 or fewer such records; the rarity screen is computed over all of data, including major areas 9+ that the station table already excluded, so the population used to define rarity is wider than the population analysed; the pull that carries the species vector to the filter is absorbed
settings: threshold n <= 5, applied to number of positive records not to number of individuals; occurrences counted over the whole unfiltered catch table
na_behavior: dplyr's tally sums the weight with na.rm = TRUE, so a record with missing catch is counted as non-positive and is indistinguishable from a true zero; a species observed only in records with missing catch would be treated as having zero occurrences and dropped
notes: The code up to this point was copied and pasted from the "b" code. I made some changes, but I confirmed they didn't affect the outputs.

section: 2 Sample x species matrix with zeros
grain_in: one row per catch record (sample_id x species_code)
grain_out: one row per haul (sample_id), one column per retained species
operation: Sums catch to one total per haul and species, then reshapes to a haul-by-species matrix filling structural gaps with zero; the pivot itself is absorbed as a reshape but values_fill = 0 is a decision recorded here; the region's true last line is the names_prefix argument, which cannot be an anchor because it carries a trailing comment
settings: sum(catch) with no na.rm; values_fill = 0; names_prefix = sp_
na_behavior: sum() without na.rm returns NA for a haul-species combination containing any missing catch, so an NA total can survive; values_fill only fills combinations absent from the long table, so a filled 0 (species not recorded in that haul) and an observed 0 catch are already indistinguishable at this point
notes: The code up to this point was copied and pasted from the "b" code. I made some changes, but I confirmed they didn't affect the outputs.

section: 2 Sample x species matrix with zeros
grain_in: one row per haul that appears in the catch table
grain_out: one row per station sampling occasion (sample_id x major_area x year x month), one column per retained species
operation: Starts from every station occasion in areas 1:8 and left joins the haul-by-species matrix, so hauls that exist in station but have no bagseine rows enter as all-zero rows; the region's true first statement is final_df_wide <- station %>%, which cannot be an anchor because it carries a trailing comment, and the distinct() is absorbed as deduplication of the station frame
settings: left_join by sample_id (station side kept); replace_na(x, 0) across all sp_ columns
na_behavior: Three different causes collapse into the same 0 after this node: a species genuinely absent from a sampled haul, a station occasion with no catch record at all (gear failure, unprocessed sample, or a join key mismatch), and an NA total produced upstream by a missing catch value; nothing downstream can tell them apart
notes: The code up to this point was copied and pasted from the "b" code. I made some changes, but I confirmed they didn't affect the outputs.

section: Period scheme: 11 periods, all 3-year bins over 1992-2024
grain_out: one row per calendar year, 1992 to 2024
operation: Defines the time binning and builds a year to period lookup of 11 consecutive 3-year bins; the stopifnot is absorbed as a consistency check on the bin widths, and period_is_partial is set to FALSE for every year and is never used downstream
settings: start_year 1992; end_year 2024; period_lengths rep(3, 11); factor levels P1 to P11 fixed in order; bins are calendar-year, so a period boundary falls between December and January
na_behavior: No missing values are produced here, but any year outside 1992-2024 has no row, so a later join on year yields NA period for it
notes: The code up to this point was copied and pasted from the "b" code. I made some changes, but I confirmed they didn't affect the outputs.

grain_in: one row per station sampling occasion, one column per retained species
grain_out: one row per station sampling occasion x species (sample_id x major_area x year x month x period x season x species_code)
operation: Restricts to the years covered by the period scheme, attaches period, unpivots the species columns and assigns a season label from month; the pivot_longer, the species_code recast and the mid-month date are absorbed as reshaping and derived labels, while the year filter and the season assignment change which stratum a row belongs to; the final filter is described in the code as safety and is a no-op because the year filter above it already guarantees a matching period
settings: year >= 1992 and year <= 2024; left_join by year; seasons DJF, MAM, JJA, SON, so December is grouped with the January and February of the same calendar year rather than the following ones; date set to the 15th of the month; season factor level order Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall
na_behavior: A month outside 1:12 or a missing month falls through every case_when branch and becomes season NA; such rows are not removed here because only period NA is filtered, so they would later fail the semi_join on season and disappear without being counted; abundance NAs no longer exist at this point because they were replaced by 0 upstream
notes: The code up to this point was copied and pasted from the "b" code. I made some changes, but I confirmed they didn't affect the outputs.

grain_in: one row per station sampling occasion (sample_id x major_area x year x month)
grain_out: one row per station sampling occasion, with period and season attached
operation: Applies the same year filter, period join and season assignment to the station table so that sampling effort can be counted independently of the catch data; this is a separate node from monthly_long because the input differs, and the two copies of the season case_when must agree for the effort screen to describe the same strata as the data it screens
settings: year >= 1992 and year <= 2024; left_join keeps only year and period; season branches identical to monthly_long; the season factor levels are written without spaces here, which is cosmetic only
na_behavior: Same collapse as monthly_long: a missing or out-of-range month yields season NA and the row survives the period filter, so it would be counted into a stratum keyed on NA season rather than being flagged

grain_in: one row per station sampling occasion
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season (major_area x period x season)
operation: Counts the distinct sample_ids observed in each bay by period by season cell, giving the realised sampling effort that the next node screens on
settings: grouping major_area x period x season; effort measured as distinct sample_id, so repeated rows for one sample cannot inflate it
na_behavior: A cell with no sampling at all produces no row rather than a row with n_samples = 0, so a stratum that was never sampled and a stratum that was sampled but failed the threshold are not distinguishable in this table

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season with a sample count
grain_out: one row per retained bay x period x season
operation: Keeps only strata whose sample count is exactly 180 so that all retained strata carry identical effort, which is what stands in for rarefaction; the message is absorbed as reporting; 180 is not derived anywhere in the code, so what one row means depends on an unstated design (3 years x 3 months x 20 samples per bay-month?) that should be confirmed against the sampling protocol
settings: equality test n_samples == 180, not >=, so a stratum with 181 or more samples is dropped along with undersampled ones; the retained set varies by period and season, so different periods can rest on different bays
na_behavior: No NA is produced, but the reason a stratum was dropped (undersampled, oversampled, or never sampled and therefore absent) is not recorded; the message reports only two totals

section: Restrict monthly data to fully sampled strata
grain_in: one row per station sampling occasion x species
grain_out: one row per station sampling occasion x species, restricted to fully sampled strata
operation: Drops every observation belonging to a bay by period by season cell that did not carry exactly 180 samples, which is the filter that defines the population all three diversity tables describe
settings: semi_join on major_area, period and season; no columns added
na_behavior: Rows whose season is NA cannot match any key and are dropped here silently, together with rows from genuinely undersampled strata; the two causes are not separated and no count of dropped rows is produced

section: 4. Compute diversity metrics (observed only; no rarefaction)
grain_in: one row per sampling occasion x species within one group
grain_out: one named numeric vector per group, one element per species code present in the group
units_out: individuals pooled over all occasions in the group
operation: Defines the helper that pools abundance across all sampling occasions in a group to a single species-total vector, which is the community each diversity index is then computed on; the definition is one node, and its two call sites (alpha_div and gamma_div) are the separate nodes below
settings: sum with no na.rm; element names come from species_code, so ordering follows sorted species codes; because zeros were carried forward, species never caught in the group appear with a total of 0 rather than being absent
na_behavior: A single missing abundance anywhere in a group makes that species' total NA, which then makes the whole group's richness and Shannon value NA; after the upstream zero fill no NAs should reach here, so an NA appearing at this point would indicate a fault earlier in the pipeline rather than a sparse stratum

section: 4. Compute diversity metrics: alpha-diversity (bay x P x S)
end_anchor: select(period, season, major_area, richness, shannon, hill_shannon)
grain_in: one row per sampling occasion x species within retained strata
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season (major_area x period x season)
units_out: species count (richness), Shannon entropy in nats, effective number of species (hill_shannon)
operation: Pools abundance to a species-total vector per bay by period by season and calls vegan to get observed richness and Shannon entropy, then exponentiates to the Hill number of order 1; the list-column of community vectors is absorbed as an intermediate that only carries the pooled vector to the two vegan calls, and the closing select is absorbed as column pruning; the header states these are observed values with no rarefaction, which rests on the effort screen at valid_strata rather than on anything done here
settings: grouping period x season x major_area; across(everything()) passes all remaining columns into build_comm; vegan::specnumber counts elements greater than zero, so the carried zeros do not inflate richness; vegan::diversity with index = shannon uses natural logarithms, so hill_shannon = exp(H) is on the same base; no rarefaction, no coverage standardisation
na_behavior: specnumber and diversity both return NA for a community vector containing any NA, so a single missing abundance turns the entire stratum's richness, shannon and hill_shannon into NA; that NA is not distinguishable downstream from a stratum that was retained but had no fish, which would instead give richness 0 and shannon 0 with hill_shannon 1

section: 4. Compute diversity metrics: gamma-diversity (pooled across bays)
grain_in: one row per sampling occasion x species within retained strata
grain_out: one row per period x season
units_out: species count (richness), Shannon entropy in nats, effective number of species (hill_shannon)
operation: Repeats the same pooling and the same two vegan calls with bay dropped from the grouping, giving the regional pool for each period by season; it is a separate node from alpha_div because what one row represents differs, and because the pooled area is whatever set of bays passed the 180-sample screen for that cell, the region described by gamma can change from one period or season to the next
settings: grouping period x season only; across(everything()) into build_comm; specnumber and diversity as in alpha_div; index = shannon (natural log); hill_shannon = exp(H)
na_behavior: Same collapse as alpha_div: any NA abundance makes the whole period by season value NA, indistinguishable from a genuinely empty pool; a period by season with no retained bays produces no row at all rather than an NA row

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season
grain_out: one row per period x season
units_in: species count and effective number of species
units_out: mean species count and mean effective number of species across retained bays
operation: Averages the bay-level richness and Hill-Shannon values within each period by season to form the alpha term of the multiplicative beta; the mean is unweighted across bays, so a period by season resting on three retained bays is averaged the same way as one resting on eight
settings: arithmetic (not geometric) mean; na.rm = TRUE on both means; no weighting by bay area or by abundance; shannon itself is not averaged, only hill_shannon, so the Hill scale is used for the diversity term
na_behavior: na.rm = TRUE silently drops any bay whose alpha was NA, so the divisor for that cell is a mean over fewer bays and no record of how many bays contributed is kept; if every bay in a cell were NA the mean would be NaN rather than NA

grain_in: one row per period x season, mean alpha side; one row per period x season, gamma side
grain_out: one row per period x season
units_in: species count, effective number of species
operation: Joins the regional values to the mean local values and divides to give multiplicative beta on two scales, richness (Hill order 0) and Hill-Shannon (order 1), so both ratios are on the same Hill footing despite the different column names; the rename inside the join is absorbed as disambiguation and the transmute is absorbed as column selection
settings: left_join by period and season, mean-alpha side kept; beta_richness = gamma richness / mean alpha richness; beta_shannon = gamma hill_shannon / mean alpha hill_shannon; no lower bound of 1 is imposed and no correction for unequal numbers of bays is applied, so a cell averaged over three bays and one averaged over eight are reported on the same axis
na_behavior: Four different causes collapse into a non-finite or missing beta and none is labelled: a period by season present in alpha but absent from gamma gives NA through the join, an NA on either side propagates, a mean alpha of exactly 0 gives Inf, and 0 divided by 0 gives NaN; only the mean_alpha side controls which rows exist, so a gamma row with no matching alpha row is dropped without notice

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season, or per period x season
grain_out: unchanged; three CSV files on disk
operation: Writes the three tables to a results folder beside the script; no quantity changes meaning here, and the node is included only so a reviewer can check that each table lands in the file its name claims; the directory creation and the date tag are absorbed as housekeeping
settings: output directory created if absent; filenames carry today's date, so a rerun on a different day writes new files rather than overwriting, and the results folder accumulates versions with no marker of which one is current; file prefixes are L5_alpha, L5_gamma and L5_beta
na_behavior: Nothing is written if an upstream object is missing, in which case the script errors rather than producing a partial file; NA values in the tables are written as empty fields by write_csv and are not distinguishable in the file from a value that was never computed
